question: When is a delivery considered late?
answer: “Late deliveries are defined as arriving more than three days after the estimate.” [1]

passages.heading: Measuring Delivery Delays in Online Retail › Abstract
passages.text: We study how long parcels take to arrive and how often they are lost. Late deliveries are defined as arriving more than three days after the estimate.
passages.snippet: study how long parcels take to arrive and how often they are lost. Late deliveries are defined as arriving more than three days after the estimate

passages.heading: Measuring Delivery Delays in Online Retail › 1 Introduction
passages.text: Online retailers promise delivery windows that customers rely on. When a parcel is late, the customer contacts support, and the cost of that contact often exceeds the margin on the order. This paper measures delays across carriers and seasons. We find that most delays cluster in December, when volumes double and sorting centres run at capacity.

passages.heading: Measuring Delivery Delays in Online Retail › 3 Results
passages.text: The median delay was zero days, but the distribution has a long tail: five per cent of parcels arrived more than a week late. Economy services were four times as likely to be late as tracked services. Losses were rare, at roughly one parcel in two hundred.

passages.heading: Measuring Delivery Delays in Online Retail › 2 Data
passages.text: The dataset covers 120,000 shipments sent between January and December. Each record contains the dispatch date, the promised window, the delivery date and the carrier. Shipments without a delivery scan were treated as lost after fifteen working days.
